---
title: "Load Asset"
subtitle: "Compare your own assembly against the catalogue"
---

**Load Asset** lets you bring your own data into the discovery platform. You upload a packaged analysis of an assembly, and the platform projects its clusters into the catalogue so you can see them in the roster and on the maps alongside everything else — scored and positioned the same way as catalogue iBGCs.

This replaces the older "upload and evaluate" workflow: instead of a separate evaluation page, your clusters become first-class iBGCs in the same discovery platform you already use.

## What you upload

A **packaged assembly analysis** as a `.tar.gz` (or `.tgz`) archive. This is the bundle produced by the annotation pipeline ([How the Data Is Built](how-data-is-built.qmd)) for a single assembly — the same per-assembly output that catalogue data is loaded from. If you have run your genome or metagenome through that pipeline, the package is ready to upload.

The upload is small and intended for one assembly at a time.

## What happens after upload

1. The file uploads and the projection runs as a background job — the chip shows **queued** then **projecting**. Large assets can take a few minutes; keep the tab open.
2. When it finishes, your clusters appear as iBGCs flagged **SUBMITTED** (shown in amber) at the top of the [roster](bgc-roster.qmd) and as points on the [Variables map](variables-map.qmd) and [UMAP](umap.qmd).
3. Each submitted iBGC is **projected** against the catalogue's clustering: it is assigned to the nearest gene cluster family and given novelty and domain-novelty scores, so you can read it against catalogue clusters directly.

The chip shows the assembly accession and the number of iBGCs projected. Hover it for the organism name.

## Working with a loaded asset

- Submitted iBGCs behave like any other: left-click to inspect, right-click to set as reference, find similar, or add to a shortlist.
- The asset stays loaded as you switch result tabs and **survives Run Query**, so you can filter and search the catalogue while keeping your clusters in view for comparison.
- A natural workflow is to **set one of your submitted iBGCs as the reference**, then [Find similar iBGCs](similar-ibgc.qmd) to pull up the catalogue clusters most like it.

## Limits and privacy

- **One asset at a time.** Loading a new file replaces the previous one.
- **Ephemeral.** The upload is held only for your session and is evicted when you remove it (the **×** on the chip) or after it expires. It is never added to the public catalogue or shared with other users.
- If the platform has no clustering run available to project against, the asset still loads but its clusters are shown un-projected (the chip notes this).
